validated_work_order.understanding:
Issue #51 collects four non-blocking findings the review of PR #50 raised and approved despite, plus asks that each be re-checked before it is planned. I reproduced all four against this checkout at 07406d2 rather than inheriting the previous plan's numbers, and corrected two of them where the review and the previous plan were themselves wrong.

(1) REPRODUCED, and the evidence is sharper than the review's. packages/loot-core/src/platform/server/sqlite/index.test.ts:35 — the afterEach added by PR #50 calls vi.restoreAllMocks(), which is file-scoped rather than spy-scoped: it restores every spy the file holds, including the global.fetch spy that patchFetchForSqlJS installs in the top-level beforeAll (index.test.ts:17, implemented as vi.spyOn(global, 'fetch').mockImplementation(...) at packages/loot-core/src/mocks/util.ts:71). I probed it by appending `it('PROBE_FETCH', () => console.error('PROBE fetch isMock=' + vi.isMockFunction(globalThis.fetch)))` to the describe, twice, in two positions:
  - Probe LAST (after the eight other tests, so at least one afterEach has run): prints 'PROBE fetch isMock=false'. The spy really is gone.
  - Probe FIRST: prints 'PROBE fetch isMock=true' — a false pass, because no afterEach has run yet. This is a finding the previous plan asserted without checking and it matters: it is the same over-claim this ticket exists to remove, and it is why the new regression test must be positioned last.
The suite stays green in both positions ('Tests 16 passed (16)') because init() runs once in the beforeAll and sql.js caches the compiled wasm — latent, exactly as the review said. The proposed fix works: hoisting baseURL to module scope, keeping patchFetchForSqlJS(baseURL) in the beforeAll for init(), and adding a top-level beforeEach that re-arms it turns the last-position probe into 'PROBE fetch isMock=true'. Removing only that four-line beforeEach and re-running turns it back to false. Both directions run on this checkout; the working tree was restored (git status shows only the untracked plan/ directory).

The sibling is packages/loot-core/src/platform/server/fs/index.test.ts (NOT sqlite/fs/index.test.ts — no such directory exists; the previous plan cited that path twice). Its beforeAll at fs/index.test.ts:18-22 installs the same patchFetchForSqlJS(baseURL), and its afterEach at fs/index.test.ts:28-30 calls only sqlite._getModule().reset_filesystem() with no vi.restoreAllMocks(), so its fetch patch survives every test. It is not a counterexample to the fix; it is the shape that has no bug, and it must stay unchanged.

(2) REPRODUCED. packages/loot-core/src/platform/server/sqlite/index.electron.test.ts:143 — the comment block at lines 142-144 says `expect(handles).toHaveLength(0)` is 'above'. That assertion is at line 151, after teardown() at line 148. `grep -n 'expect(handles).toHaveLength(0)'` on that file returns exactly two hits, 143 and 151, in that order. One word is wrong.

(3) REPRODUCED, and this is the objection the last plan's rejection raised — the comment at index.test.ts:28-31 over-claims on BOTH halves, not one. grep on this checkout gives:
  - nine `it(` blocks, opening at 41, 70, 110, 150, 198, 219, 260, 325, 381;
  - ten `await openDatabase()` calls at 42, 71, 111, 154, 199, 220, 261, 341, 344, 382;
  - `handles.push` at only 342 and 345, both inside the block opening at 325, 'should report an unparseable pattern once per database handle, not once per process';
  - `spyOn(console` at five sites — 52, 87, 131, 282, 350 — mapping into the blocks opening at 41, 70, 110, 260 and 325. The four blocks opening at 150 ('should use the crdt index for a batched cell lookup'), 198 ('should match regex on text fields'), 219 ('should not throw on an unparseable regex, matching nothing instead') and 381 ('should still match a valid regex that does match, and not throw on one that does not') never mock console.log at all.
  So the handle half is true of ONE test of nine, and the mock half of FIVE tests of nine — not 'every test'. The current comment asserts both unrestrictedly ('would skip the cleanup and leave an open handle and a mocked console.log behind for the next test'), so both halves must be narrowed. The sibling electron file's comment (lines 23-26) needs no narrowing and must not be touched: all three of its tests both mock console.log and push a handle (52/55, 82-86/89, 139-141/146), so there its claim is true of every test.
  Two corrections to the review's and the previous plan's own arithmetic, which I re-derived rather than copied: the review says 'The six vi.spyOn(console, log) sites ... (index.test.ts:50, 85, 129, 280, 348)' — six claimed, five listed, five actual; and `grep -n 'vi\.spyOn(console'` matches only FOUR lines (52, 131, 282, 350), because the site at 87 is a wrapped `.spyOn(console, 'log')` on its own line under a trailing `vi`. The grep that finds all five is `grep -n 'spyOn(console'`. The rejection's own prescribed grep, `vi\.spyOn\(console`, would have returned four and been read as 'four tests mock console'. AC-4 uses the pattern that actually finds five and says so.

(4) NOT A CODE CHANGE. gh pr view 50 on this checkout: state MERGED, title 'fix: Follow-ups from #35: 5 from the review' — no [AI] prefix, against the mandatory prefix in .github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md. PR #50 is merged, so no diff can carry this fix; the rule is enforced at PR creation and .github/** is a forbidden path. The review notes PRs 37, 39, 40 and 49 share the shape, which makes it a pipeline-wide habit rather than this ticket's code. Deferred to a human with the reason recorded.
validated_work_order.root_cause: PR #50 added a blanket vi.restoreAllMocks() to index.test.ts's afterEach and, separately, wrote a comment that claims more than the code does. The blanket restore reaches beyond the console spy AC-1 targeted because vi.restoreAllMocks() is file-scoped rather than spy-scoped, so it silently takes the file's global.fetch spy down with it after the first test. The comment was written from the shape of the teardown rather than from what the tests actually register: it speaks of 'a mocked console.log' as though all nine tests mocked one (five do) and of 'an open handle' as though every openDatabase() handle were closed (one test pushes any). Both halves of one sentence over-generalised the same way, which is why both are narrowed here rather than only the handle half.
validated_work_order.approach:
Three small edits across the two files PR #50 touched, plus one regression test that fails without the fix.

The fetch patch moves from once-per-file to once-per-test. Hoist the existing baseURL template literal (currently computed inside the beforeAll at index.test.ts:16) to a module-scope const, keep patchFetchForSqlJS(baseURL) in the beforeAll where init({ baseURL }) needs it, and add a top-level beforeEach that calls patchFetchForSqlJS(baseURL) again. patchFetchForSqlJS is vi.spyOn(global, 'fetch').mockImplementation(...) with no internal restore, so re-spying a restored global is idempotent and the afterEach's blanket restore can no longer outrun it. This is the smaller of the two fixes the review offered; the other, narrowing the restore to the console spy alone, would mean hand-tracking which spies exist at teardown time and would break the deliberate mirroring of index.electron.test.ts's teardown().

A new test appended at the end of the describe asserts vi.isMockFunction(globalThis.fetch) is true. It must not be placed first, and this is now verified rather than asserted: I ran a probe in both positions on this checkout and a first-positioned probe reports 'PROBE fetch isMock=true' even with the defect present, because no afterEach has run yet — it would pass for the wrong reason and be vacuous under -t filtering. A comment on the test must say so, matching the existing convention in index.electron.test.ts:129-137.

The comment at index.test.ts:28-31 is rewritten so each half carries its true scope, and BOTH halves are narrowed — this is the correction the last plan's rejection demanded, and it applies in four places (.understanding, .approach, files[0].change, AC-4), all corrected below. The restore half is scoped to the tests that mock console.log (five of nine) rather than to every test; the close half is scoped to the one test that pushes handles. The exact text of the replacement comment is written out in files[0].change so the implementer does not have to choose wording.

In index.electron.test.ts:143 'above' becomes 'below'. One word, and that file's own comment at lines 23-26 is deliberately left alone because there both claims are true of every test.

No production code changes. No new dependency. No behaviour change outside the test files.
